1.point: Open from the prayer's image of sleep, move to death and the common picture of the dead as far away, and announce that this chapter will show, through the soul and its worlds, that what the soul becomes is in our hands.
steps: Read the opening quotation: sleep as a picture of neglect, set beside meeting God
Move from the sleep image to real sleep, death and the popular picture of barzakh as a distant waiting room
State the chapter's claim (the dead go nowhere; the reason is what the soul is) and its three steps

2.point: Reality has three worlds that are depths of one world, not separate places, so the dead in barzakh have gone deeper, not away.
steps: The soul is a copy of creation, so our three ways of knowing sample three worlds
Senses sample the material world; the other two are unseen but not distant
Imagination samples the world of images: form without matter, existing outside any mind
Intellect samples the world of intellects: meaning without image
The world of images stands between the other two and is therefore barzakh
The worlds are dimensions of one reality, differing in depth not distance
So the dead in barzakh are deeper in this world, not elsewhere

3.point: The soul is not fixed to one world: its hold on the body loosens in sleep, death and contemplation, and unlike an angel its reach is set by the life it lives.
steps: The soul has a share in each world because it was made to link spirit and body
For now the body holds its attention; that hold loosens at three times
Sleep: the soul touches the world of images
Death: the hold lets go entirely and the soul goes on in the image body
Contemplation: attention turned to God loosens the hold on purpose
Angels have fixed stations; the human soul does not
So how far the soul goes depends on the life it lives

4.point: The deeds we do now shape the image body the soul will wear after death.
steps: Objection: if every soul enters the middle world anyway, do deeds matter?
Repeated acts shape the self (habit)
That shaping shows faintly on the face here and strongly on the image body
The form is settled at the moment the soul departs
Scriptural pictures and the principle that rewards are the deeds made manifest confirm it
So the image body is being shaped now by what we do

5.point: The self that does the deeds is one self with three states and can rise from commanding evil to peace, so what the soul becomes is, with God's grace, in our hands.
steps: If deeds shape the form, the self is not fixed either
The Qur'an's three names for the self are three states: commanding to evil, self-blaming, at peace
They are one self, not three, so the state can be changed
Familiar acts move it: remembrance, fasting, night prayer
They work because the soul takes on habits quickly and is entrusted to us
So what the soul becomes is, by God's grace, in our hands

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Reads the opening quotation and sets up sleep as the picture of neglect beside the meeting with God, the hook the section needs.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Moves from sleep as metaphor to real sleep, death and the popular picture of barzakh as a distant waiting room, the misconception the chapter will overturn.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: States the chapter's claim in the Sheikh's words, grounds it in the soul, and announces the three steps; this is the section's point.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Supplies the premise (the soul is a copy of creation) and the method (three ways of knowing sample three worlds) that the whole section runs on.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: First world via the senses, and plants the key qualification that unseen means untrained eye, not far away, which ¶10 and ¶12 depend on.

¶6.label: support
¶6.why: The example of the imagined face and the dream is what ¶7 draws the world of images from; without it ¶7's 'like the picture in our mind' has no referent.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Second world: form without matter, existing outside any mind. New step.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Third world via the intellect: meaning without image or matter. New step.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Places the world of images between the other two and names it barzakh, the link that lets ¶12 relocate the dead.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Turns three worlds into depths of one world rather than places; the step the point most needs.

¶11.label: restate
¶11.why: Summarises ¶5-¶10 and repeats 'none of them is far away' from ¶5 and ¶10; adds no link.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Lands the point: the dead in barzakh are deeper, not away. The resurrection sentence is an extra not needed here but the paragraph's job is the conclusion.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Establishes that the soul has a share in each world because it was made to link spirit and body; the premise for its movement.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: States the present condition (body holds attention) and names the three loosenings the section will take in turn.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: First loosening, sleep; the dream of the future is the evidence that the soul reaches the middle world.

¶16.label: support
¶16.why: A two-sentence lead-in to the verse that ¶17 reads; the sleep-death pairing itself was already made in ¶2, so this only serves as a hinge and could be folded into ¶17.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: Second loosening, death, as a difference of degree, and introduces the image body that Section 4 will need.

¶18.label: restate
¶18.why: Its claim, that at death the soul goes on in the image body, was made in ¶17; the 'soul carries the body' quotation reframes it attractively but adds no step the point uses.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Third loosening, contemplation, with the muraqaba evidence; needed to complete the three named in ¶14.

¶20.label: restate
¶20.why: Summarises ¶15-¶19; 'three ways of loosening one hold' was already set out in ¶14.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: Introduces the contrast with angels, whose station is fixed; needed for the 'as far as its life takes it' half of the point.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Lands the point: the soul's reach is not fixed and depends on the life lived.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: Raises the objection (do deeds matter if everyone enters the middle world?) and answers with habit shaping the self, the first step.

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: Carries the shaping from face to image body: sin deforms, piety makes it shine. This is the section's point, stated here first.

¶25.label: support
¶25.why: Imam Khomeini corroborates the second form and supplies the moment that fixes it (departure of the soul), which ¶28 relies on. The al-Naba lead-in starts a shift to the Last Day body.

¶26.label: aside
¶26.why: A hadith and a second verse about the Last Day, which ¶27 itself concedes is not the image body; deleting it would break nothing in the argument.

¶27.label: support
¶27.why: The first half is a Last Day digression, but Shomali's principle that rewards are the deeds made manifest is the evidence ¶28 draws on for 'the work of its own deeds'.

¶28.label: restate
¶28.why: States the conclusion already stated in ¶24; the 'our future is now present' line adds emphasis on the present tense but no new link.

¶29.label: restate
¶29.why: A recap of Sections 2-4 with nothing new; the section begins at ¶30.

¶30.label: advance
¶30.why: Draws the inference that the self is not fixed, introduces the three names as states and gives the first, the self that commands to evil.

¶31.label: support
¶31.why: Reads the Yusuf verse to name God's mercy as what overcomes the lowest self (used by the 'God's grace' in the point) and adds worry as a pull, which ¶38 picks up.

¶32.label: advance
¶32.why: Second state, the self-blaming self, and why it is hopeful.

¶33.label: advance
¶33.why: Third state, the self at peace, completing the ascent the point describes.

¶34.label: advance
¶34.why: The key step: these are one self, not three, so changing the attitude changes the state.

¶35.label: advance
¶35.why: First of the means by which the self moves, remembrance; the point needs that movement is possible by familiar acts.

¶36.label: support
¶36.why: The shared root between the verse's 'rest' and mutma'inna ties remembrance to the third state named in ¶33.

¶37.label: support
¶37.why: Two further means, fasting and night prayer, tied back to the loosening of Section 3; ¶38's 'these acts' needs more than one, though the Ramadan light detail is more than the step requires.

¶38.label: advance
¶38.why: Explains why the acts work (habit) and introduces the soul as entrusted to us, the step the conclusion rests on.

¶39.label: restate
¶39.why: A chapter summary; the one new clause, that the drive to begin is itself God's grace, has not been prepared and is the only part doing work. Everything else repeats ¶12, ¶20, ¶28 and ¶34.

¶40.label: aside
¶40.why: Raises a question the chapter does not answer; a bridge to the next chapter, not a link in this section's chain.
